text: Every evening, the sea asks the same question.
I put on the coat. I bank the stove. I answer.
My father rowed this water. His father cut these steps.
The crossing is short. It only feels like a life.
Halfway out, the sun lets go of the day.
And the water holds the last of it, the way I hold his name.
The tower waits. It has never once waited badly.
One match. One wick. One turn of the little wheel.
And the light goes out across the water — so nobody else has to ask.
